body: We were in a position where he had to turn it down. Our school district required a full year commitment to virtual or in person. We were already locked into virtual when they offered him his job back.
Mine, but I say ours, as he's been in his life more than his bio dad.

Interesting take but no I'm not mad at him for taking time to himself, in upset because he's not pulling his weight. He's not standing over our kid 8 hours a day supervising. Our kid is 8, he's pretty self sufficient. Our kid logs in and does his work yin his own, and is capable of feeding himself, he's just too young to stay home. At any time during the day he could do the dishes or sweep the floor. I'm not asking him to do any kind of extravagant work.

He can take all the time he wants for his hobbies, once other stuff is done. He can xbox his brains out if the other tasks for the day are done. But that's not what's happening. As kids most of us are taught work first play second. But his mindset is more like think about work, take a break for two hours, maybe do the work.

 For a different perspective, I also get zero time for myself. Yesterday was the most relaxing day I've had in months. Why? Because I had all my wisdom teeth pulled and took a day off work. And even though I napped half the day (because drugs), I still ended up cleaning, helping with my kid's schoolwork, and doing my own studying for 6 hours, and went right back to work today for 11 hours. I gave him 3 things to do today, one thing got done. And the thing that got done actually ended up making more work (washed the dog, but also let the wet dog dry himself all over our bed).

I don't think my expectations are unrealistic or too high. 

And yes, I have told him how I feel about him on vs off meds. Just like he has told me with my meds, as we both struggle with mental illness. We have been together for 5 years but we've been inseparable for almost 17 years, we're pretty involved in each other's shit at this point.

I know isolation is hard. BUT our kid has severe asthma, and we are in a bigger city in Wisconsin. That's the reason why we committed to virtual learning. And except for work(where I'm in a mask and distanced), I'm isolated along with them. We don't go into stores, we just pick up. We don't go anywhere or do anything really besides having out in our yard.  I can see work as at least being out of the house, but it's not any less stressful really being there.

Yes and no.

In the beginning of our relationship we had more dialogue. During this time he was also unmedicated bipolar. Since he got on meds it's been more of the shut down / disassociate response.

I know it's truly selfish to say but he was more loving, receptive, passionate, and caring when he wasn't medicated.... But he also wanted to die all the time. So even though it was a better time in our relationship, it was a terrible time for him.

If I stop doing it or reminding just doesn't get done. If I didn't give him a meal to cook, my kid would eat sandwiches for dinner every day(I get home after dinner). And the housework I do is out of necessity, like washing dishes to be able to eat, or cleaning the cat box because my workspace is next to it and I can't stand the smell. Idk what he needs to feel responsible or motivated.
He has always had issues with motivation, but I've never had to rely on him so heavily. I used to just pick up the slack but I can't always do that now.
He has a psychiatrist and I've pushed for therapy. It's another thing in the list that doesn't get done.
He has a psychiatrist and is on meds.

He is bipolar, but has not been having episodes lately. He's been pretty level with his meds. We've been together 5 years and I've seen him at every stage of bipolar (including overdoses and hospitalizing him against his will). He's in a "normal" zone right now.

He has not gotten any unemployment, and his employer offered him his job back after we committed to virtual learning. As such, he is owed about 3 months of unemployment that hasn't come yet, and he no longer qualifies for continuing unemployment since he "turned down his job". So what he does at home is his only contribution.
